title: OpenAI and Anthropic poach Trump officials as industry fights for Washington’s trust
gist: Anthropic and OpenAI are hiring former Trump administration officials for board, compute-strategy, national-security and strategy roles as frontier AI becomes a national security issue and the White House shows it will use procurement, supply-chain designations and export controls as leverage. The 'Anthropic episode', in which an appeals court upheld a Pentagon supply-chain-risk designation, is cited as the lesson driving labs to court Washington ahead of potential record IPOs.

insights.claim: In 2026 Anthropic appointed at least two former Trump officials, Chris Liddell to its board in February and ex-OSTP adviser Sihao Huang as head of frontier compute strategy in September, while OpenAI hired at least three officials from Trump's administrations.
insights.speaker: Kai Nicol-Schwarz
insights.so_what: Frontier labs are investing in political capital as government becomes a key determinant of their business outcomes.

insights.claim: CNAS fellow Michelle Nie Duncan says frontier AI companies know the Trump administration has many levers over their business, from federal procurement and supply-chain designations to export controls, and is willing to use them.
insights.speaker: Kai Nicol-Schwarz
insights.so_what: Regulatory and political risk is a material valuation factor for AI labs and their partners.
insights.quote: “Frontier AI companies are aware that the Trump administration has a lot of levers over their business, from federal procurement and supply-chain designations to export controls and everything in between, and that it’s willing to use them,”

insights.claim: A US appeals court in September upheld a Pentagon designation of Anthropic as a supply chain risk following a public dispute between the two earlier in the year, which other labs have taken as a lesson to stay on the White House's good side.
insights.speaker: Kai Nicol-Schwarz
insights.so_what: Government designations can directly restrict an AI lab's federal market access, a key risk for Anthropic investors.
insights.quote: “They have learned from the Anthropic episode that it pays to be on the good side of the White House,”
insights.locator: They have learned from the Anthropic episode

insights.claim: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has tried to smooth relations with Trump after an antagonistic year, joining a lunch between Trump and AI bosses and dining with Trump in September.
insights.speaker: Kai Nicol-Schwarz
insights.so_what: A thaw could reduce Anthropic's federal regulatory and procurement risk.

insights.claim: Trump has called AI safety concerns a 'hoax' and favored self-regulation by AI companies, while also saying the Department of Justice and other law enforcement bodies could rein in AI.
insights.speaker: Kai Nicol-Schwarz
insights.so_what: Mixed signals mean enforcement risk for AI firms remains discretionary and politically driven.

insights.claim: OpenAI hired Thomas Lind from the Office of the National Cyber Director to lead cyber and strategic risk, Dean Ball, a drafter of America's AI Action Plan, as head of strategic futures, and former HHS chief AI officer Peter Bowman-Davis for model training and hardware engineering.
insights.speaker: Kai Nicol-Schwarz
entities: Office of the National Cyber Director
insights.so_what: OpenAI is building a national-security policy bench, positioning for government contracts and policy influence.

insights.claim: Nie Duncan argues that because OpenAI and Anthropic are preparing for some of the largest IPOs ever and can pay more than the public sector, officials see the AI labs as where real leverage over AI governance now lies.
insights.speaker: Kai Nicol-Schwarz
insights.so_what: Signals expected mega-IPOs from frontier labs and a drain of policy talent from government.
insights.quote: “The AI labs are becoming some of the most consequential institutions in the world, and for officials who are serious about shaping the future of AI governance, inside the labs is where a lot of leverage currently lies.”

insights.claim: Anthropic has been racing to sign AI data center deals and struck a roughly $45 billion cloud deal with neocloud Nscale, CNBC reported in August.
insights.speaker: Kai Nicol-Schwarz
insights.so_what: Neocloud providers are capturing large frontier-lab compute contracts.
insights.locator: Anthropic has been racing to ink AI data center deals

insights.claim: Apollo and several banks are reportedly in talks to finance SpaceX's $40 billion purchase of Nvidia GPUs.
insights.speaker: Kai Nicol-Schwarz
insights.so_what: Private credit is becoming a major financier of GPU purchases, adding leverage to the AI buildout.

insights.claim: Google was ordered to halt work on two data centers in Finland a month after committing to invest $15 billion in AI infrastructure there.
insights.speaker: Kai Nicol-Schwarz
insights.so_what: Local permitting and regulatory pushback is a growing risk to hyperscaler data center timelines in Europe.

insights.claim: A Ukrainian drone strike forced Russian internet company Yandex to suspend operations at one of its key data centers.
insights.speaker: Kai Nicol-Schwarz
insights.so_what: Data centers are now military targets, adding physical risk to digital infrastructure in conflict zones.

insights.claim: AI agent startup Manus raised more than $500 million in its first funding round since Meta was forced to abandon its acquisition of the company.
insights.speaker: Kai Nicol-Schwarz
insights.so_what: Blocked AI acquisitions are pushing targets back to private capital markets.

insights.claim: Microsoft's market cap is approaching $4 trillion, but almost four years into the AI boom it has yet to find a breakout hit at the model or application layer.
insights.speaker: Kai Nicol-Schwarz
insights.so_what: Raises questions about Microsoft's AI monetization beyond cloud infrastructure.
